newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Mandela pledges to promote solar use regionally.
newsitem.headline: Mandela pledges to promote solar use regionally.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela on Tuesday added his voice to political pledges to back an ambitious global solar plan to bring energy to 2.4 billion people living without elecricity worldwide.

Mandela -- who missed the two-day World Solar Summit held in Harare -- said in a message to the meeting that as chairman of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) he would bring his influence to bear to ensure the regional grouping adapted its energy programmes to include renewable powers.

"In my capacity as the current chairperson of the Southern African Development Community, it is my intention to play an active role in promoting the fundamental objectives of the World Solar Summit through, inter-alia, the SADC energy protocol," he said.

Mandela pledged South Africa's cooperation and participation in implementing a United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organistion programme aiming to promote the use of solar, wind and other renewable energy sources.

"It is my belief that this declaration and programme will indeed enhance our efforts to increase accessibility of energy to the masses of our people by the turn of the century and start having positive effects on our precious physical environment," he said.
